newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Dorm Authority to sell bonds in Oct and Nov.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Dorm Authority to sell bonds in Oct and Nov.

text.p: The New York Dormitory Authority got approval to sell nearly $88 million of revenue bonds in mid-October, and as much as $60 million of revenue bonds in mid-November, an agency official said on Wednesday.
The two debt offerings, which will be sold through negotiation, were approved by the Public Authorities Control Board (PACB).

St. John's University will use the almost $88 million of bonds for renovations, new computer equipment, and various other projects. Pace University will spend the approximately $60 million that it can raise on construction and equipment.
Both debt sales are subject to a yearly interest cap of 7.5 percent.

Other projects approved by the PACB include a maximum of $69.7 million of tax equipment leasing financing for hospitals and medical centers, while the Environmental Facilities Corp got the go-ahead on almost $11 million of projects.
The Urban Development Corp won approval for nearly $80 million of projects, including one advancing economic development by helping to finance a Pathmark supermarket at 125th Street in Manhattan.
